name: Aminata Diallo
headline: 19-year-old apprentice bricklayer and part-time student, Bamako, Mali
title: Evening Invitation After Work
situation: After a long day at the construction site, as Aminata is packing her trowel, Sékou approaches and says his wife has prepared a large pot of yassa poulet for the neighborhood's Korité celebration. He invites her to join his family for the meal tonight. Aminata is exhausted and planned to study for her accounting exam by lamplight. She knows that declining a meal invitation during Korité can seem rude, but she also doesn't want to spend the money on a bus fare across town or the time away from her books. She must decide whether to accept or politely decline.

context.relationship_profiles: Sékou has taught Aminata the trade over two years, trusting her with load calculations. He once lent her a textbook when he learned she was studying accounting. His wife has never met Aminata but sends greetings through him.
context.tendencies: Aminata has declined three previous social invitations this month to study, citing fatigue. She walks past food stalls without buying to save for her sister's room. She accepts only invitations that do not require an extra bus fare.
context.current_state: Her shoulders ache from hauling cement, and her right hand is blistered where the trowel handle rubbed. She has not eaten since a piece of bread at dawn. Her exam notes are tucked inside her shirt, damp with sweat.
context.immediate_memories: The smell of yassa poulet reminds her of the last Korité before her mother died, when they ate together at a neighbor's table. Sékou's phrase 'my wife has prepared' echoes the way her mother used to announce a meal.
context.reflective_memories: She remembers her mother once refusing a holiday meal because she had to restock the market stall, and later regretting the lost connection. She recalls that every time she skipped studying to socialize, she felt behind for a week.
